summary.text: Chris Smith is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 4th District, first elected in 1980 after working in his family's sporting goods business and as executive director of the New Jersey Right to Life Committee. He is a senior member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, chairs its Africa subcommittee, and, according to his House biography, has authored 68 enacted laws, including on human trafficking, autism research and veterans.

paragraphs.text: Smith was born in Rahway, New Jersey, in 1953 and, according to his House biography, grew up in Iselin.
He earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from Trenton State College (now The College of New Jersey) in 1975 and spent a semester abroad at Worcester College in England.

He worked as Director of Institutional Sales at his family-owned sporting goods company and served as Executive Director of the New Jersey Right to Life Committee; Ballotpedia also lists work on political campaigns for Democratic officials.
Smith ran for Congress as a Republican in 1978 and lost to Rep. Frank Thompson, then defeated Thompson in 1980 and took office in 1981.
He is serving his 23rd term; in the 119th Congress he is a senior member of the Foreign Affairs Committee, chairs its Africa subcommittee, and also sits on its Western Hemisphere subcommittee.

Earlier he chaired the House Veterans' Affairs Committee for two terms, beginning in January 2001, and chaired Foreign Affairs subcommittees on human rights, international operations and organizations, and global health.

He co-chairs the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission and the Congressional-Executive Commission on China, has served as Special Representative on Human Trafficking for the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly, and has chaired the Helsinki Commission (CSCE) five times.
Smith is the author of the Trafficking Victims Protection Act of 2000 and of several autism research laws, among the 68 laws his House biography credits to him.
He chairs or co-founded several bipartisan congressional caucuses, including the Pro-life, Autism, Alzheimer's, Lyme Disease and Human Trafficking caucuses.
According to his House biography, he lives in Manchester, New Jersey, with his wife, Marie.
